DETECTOR_ASYMMETRY_20260820.corollary_1: the condition (a) detector is NOT the condition (b) detector. (a) asks 'did it run' and a leak rate suffices. (b) asks 'was what it took away worth it' and MUST explicitly measure the withheld side. Writing a (b) conclusion from an (a)-scanner's output is exactly what happened to zusult this round.
DETECTOR_ASYMMETRY_20260820.corollary_2: withheld actions can only be inferred from the control arm: same-domain CAST RATE armed vs base, per-seed paired and per-game normalized -- never a single-arm count. Any suppressive id applying for promote must attach that inferred number.

DETECTOR_ASYMMETRY_20260820.rule: section 0b example 17, a new subtype on the MEASUREMENT side (the first sixteen were about an author's reasoning being voided downstream). An execution detector for a SUPPRESSIVE rule (gate/veto/withhold) can only ever see LEAKS, never HOLDS, because a withheld action emits no event. A perfectly obedient and harmful gate therefore scores perfectly on its own detector.

DETECTOR_DOMAIN_WIDER_THAN_ACTIVE_SET_20.applies_to: every arithmetic-transform id, present and future; capmono is the worked example. Flagged for the retreat/roam desire-shaping family generally.
corollaries: Every detector domain for an arithmetic gate MUST be intersected with the gate's analytic active set before the number is read.
The complement (the provably-inert sub-domain) MUST be reported alongside as a WITHIN-ARM PLACEBO -- it is free, and it is immune to the cross-seed noise that usually blocks these reads.
Upstream exemptions count: a branch that early-returns before the transform is not in the active set no matter what it bids (here bLaneKillCommit removed l1trade/l5combo entirely).
DETECTOR_DOMAIN_WIDER_THAN_ACTIVE_SET_20.general_form: For a gate that is a PURE ARITHMETIC TRANSFORM of a desire, its no-op set is solvable in CLOSED FORM from the source (here: raw>0.9 and raw<=0.72, plus every branch structurally exempted upstream). Any detector domain that straddles that boundary yields an ATTENUATED null, and an attenuated null is not evidence of no effect.
DETECTOR_DOMAIN_WIDER_THAN_ACTIVE_SET_20.pairs_with: the seventeenth example, second subtype (detector predicate STRICTER than the rule -> the rule's real domain is kept out of view). This one is the mirror image: the detector domain is WIDER than the rule's active set, so provably-inert frames are averaged in and the effect is diluted.
DETECTOR_DOMAIN_WIDER_THAN_ACTIVE_SET_20.title: Section 0b, nineteenth example (new subtype): the detector domain is WIDER than the rule's analytic active set

The 'armed 4 : base 2' null reading in the line above is also now sized: on 196 games it is 34:30 in-domain and REVERSES to 16:21 under the old resolvable filter, i.e. it was noise -- the U.0 purpose-voiding verdict stands, but the reason is that the criterion lacked resolution, not that its null was off.

abilanc_20260826.fix: The exclusion goes INSIDE the selector J.GetMostHpUnit (bots/FunLib/jmz_func.lua), next to the two exclusions of the same class already written there -- Roshan and the Tormentor. Gate resolved exactly once, turbo AND 'abilanc', threshold read from J.Site.ANCIENT_MIN_LEVEL (12, the same one campgrade/campfarm use). abilanc_20260826.opt_out: hero_doom_bringer.lua:305 (J.GetMostHpUnitAnyTier(nCreeps)). Named by MECHANISM, not by hero: it is the only consumer that reads IsAncientCreep BEFORE it commits and can ACT on an ancient (devour it when special_bonus_unique_doom_2 is trained, devour a non-ancient otherwise, fall through when it is an ancient and the talent is not). That talent's level is an engine fact this repo cannot read -- the string occurs exactly once in the tree with no talent-level table behind it -- so the collision window is not boundable from the desktop; the opt-out costs nothing and removes the question. mirana:480 mentions IsAncientCreep too but only to REJECT one after the pick, so she wants the filter, not the opt-out. SHAPE NOTE (this round's second finding): it was written as an optional parameter J.GetMostHpUnit(list, bAllowAncient) first, and the GH #188 arity ratchet went RED on all 16 files that still pass one argument -- correctly, because an optional parameter makes 'passed 1, declares 2' the shape of every existing call site. Judging those 16 rows DEFAULTED would have grown a list whose entire design is that it can only shrink. Two names cost nothing, keep every call site at 1-of-1, and put the exception in the reader's face at the call site instead of behind a bare `true`. The default name stays the guarded one, so a new call site lands on the filtered side by writing the obvious thing.

abilvalue_20260826.observation: GH #228 measured `'value'` reads on TALENT handles. This is the same key read on ORDINARY ABILITY handles. An ability's special values are keyed by the ENTRY NAME inside its AbilityValues block; in the modern long form (`"avalanche_damage" { "value" "90 180 270 360"  "special_bonus_unique_tiny" "+90" }`) `value` is an INNER key of the entry, not an entry of the ability. So GetSpecialValueInt('value') on an ability asks for an entry that does not exist and gets the documented silent 0, unless that ability literally owns an entry NAMED `value` -- which is exactly how a GENERIC talent block is written, and is why the same string answers on one family of handles and not the other.

abilvalue_20260826.the_load_bearing_reading: THE SIGN IS THE OPPOSITE OF GH #228'S, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF COUNTING IT SEPARATELY. #228's 21 sites all reduced to harmless: a hero-unique talent's bonus has no second home, so the engine must fold it into the base number the site already read, and repairing the term would DOUBLE-COUNT. abilvalue_20260826.the_obvious_repair_is_wrong_at_the_over_: The key hero_terrorblade.lua wants is `health_cost_pct`, whose KV value is 20 -- twenty PERCENT, not a fraction -- while the line multiplies by CURRENT HEALTH directly (bot:GetHealth() * <read>). Swapping the key alone turns a cost of 0 into 20x the hero's health, and the guard it feeds ((hp - cost)/maxhp > 0.5) flips from always-true to never-true: the ability would go from always permitted to never cast. The repair is two edits (`health_cost_pct` AND `/ 100`), never one. Same family as #228's lesson in the other direction: on that axis the obvious repair double-counted, on this one it inverts a guard. A claimant reading only the intended-key column would ship exactly the wrong half, so the source annotation says so and tests/test_ability_value_read_anchor.lua section 4 pins that it keeps saying so.
abilvalue_20260826.the_ordinal_is_load_bearing: A site's identity is (file, variable, nth-read-of-that-variable) -- never the line number (GH #221; this change's own annotations moved all eight lines). Every consumer is `abilityX:GetCastRange() + aetherRange` fed to an in-range test or to J.GetCastLocation, so the 25 does not waste a cast -- an out-of-range unit-target order makes the engine WALK the hero into range first -- it buys an unplanned approach toward the target on exactly the frames the decision layer believed it could act from where it stood.

alchrage_20260824.bug: Each of the four clauses was literally `DotaTime() < 30*60` (resp. 32*60) in EVERY mode. The turbo bound the author wrote decided nothing, ever, and nothing reported it -- it reads exactly like a turbo scaling somebody already did. The dead band is 15:00/16:00 to the end of a ~20-minute turbo game, i.e. a real slice of one (unlike the strategy desk's own instance in mode_farm_generic, whose 18:00-25:00 band is past the end of a turbo game). The numeric form of the same idiom, `J.IsModeTurbo() and 5*60 or 10*60` in jmz_func, is CORRECT: the discriminator is the type in the `x` slot, not the idiom.

alchrage_20260824.fix: New X.GetRageObjectiveClock(nTurboMin, nShippedMin) in both files. Gate off it returns nShippedMin*60, which is exactly what the old expression collapsed to, so gate-off equivalence is structural. The armed branch takes math.min(nClock, nTurboMin*60), so the armed predicate is a SUBSET of the shipped one whatever constants any caller passes -- a future caller handing it a turbo bound above the shipped bound still cannot widen anything. One lever.
alchrage_20260824.observation: bots/BotLib/hero_alchemist.lua and its verbatim copy bots/FunLib/rubick_hero/alchemist.lua each guarded X.ConsiderChemicalRage's Roshan and Tormentor branches with `(J.IsModeTurbo() and DotaTime() < 15*60 or DotaTime() < 30*60)` and the 16/32 twin. Lua has no ternary operator: `and` binds tighter than `or` and the `x` slot holds a COMPARISON, so it parses as `(turbo and t<15*60) or (t<30*60)`, and 15*60 < 30*60 makes the first disjunct imply the second.

arbheart_retire_20260903.declared_limit: UpdateAvailableCamp splices the FIRST camp matching EITHER `location == released.location` OR `dist(bot, camp) < 500`. When the bot itself stands inside 500u of a DIFFERENT camp that precedes the released one in the table, that other camp is retired instead. Declared rather than engineered around: the geometry this gate fires in is the bot walking TOWARD a camp an ally already holds (world fact W2 asserts dCM > 500 on the pinned frame), the wrong-camp cost is bounded by the same one-minute refresh, and it cannot latch anything. A private exact-match splice would duplicate shipped logic to buy a case no frame evidence shows.

Three outcomes, and only the first can kill an id at the desk: (a) the predicate becomes UNSATISFIABLE => the domain is structurally empty and the desk check alone is sufficient (wkreincarnmp is this case, one layer down: its 'outer branch' is the SPENDING side); (b) the predicate is forced into a NARROWER REGION => the desk check yields the SHAPE of the domain and never its emptiness, a corpus reading is still required, and that reading expires when whatever CAUSES the region changes (axeblink is this case: forced into 'Axe has an ally nearby', which is a quantity another stream is actively changing); (c) no constraint => the desk check bought nothing. ONE-LINER: a desk check can prove EMPTY, it cannot prove RARE; reading (b) as (a) writes a corpus fact into the record as a structural one. axeblink_20260819.theory: Axe's blink is not a chase tool and not an escape -- it is the delivery vehicle for Berserker's Call, and the rest of his kit is priced off the enemies the Call pins (Counter Helix procs off the attacks Call forces; Culling Blade's reset assumes a target that cannot walk away). Standard play is blink-into-Call as one motion. The cost of waiting is only the seconds left on the Call cooldown; the cost of jumping without it is the dagger's cooldown plus a death. The single-target jump is deliberately NOT held: finishing one lone hero is a fine dagger use with or without Call, so the guard keys on crowd-ness, not on Call alone.

axebuyblink_20260819.theory: Blink Dagger is the standard first big item on Axe in every mainstream build: it is not a chase or escape tool but the delivery system for Berserker's Call, and the rest of the kit is priced off the enemies the Call pins. Vanguard/Crimson Guard buy survivability but no initiation, so a melee initiator holding them can still only fight what walks into him. Turbo compresses the game to ~11 minutes, which makes a 3.6k defensive item bought before the 2.25k enabler a strictly worse ordering than in normal mode. Reachability is measured, not assumed: from Axe's own gold curves, blink bought straight after boots would have landed at 558.5 / 479.4 / 584.5s and never in the fourth game -- 3 of 4 games gain a blink with 100-240s of a decisive turbo game left, against 0 of 4 today.

axecull_preflight_20260822T1800Z.tooling_lesson: The first pass at the corpus scan was a Python regex reader and it under-counted Axe frames 10 -> 26, which would have turned a REACHED ring (3 frames) into an empty one and produced a confident wrong 'nothing reaches the branch' verdict of exactly the kind this stream keeps warning about. The published numbers come from `dofile` on each fixture -- the same loader the tests use. DO NOT re-derive corpus counts by pattern-matching fixture files.
axecull_preflight_20260822T1800Z.verdict: DO NOT WRITE THIS ROUND -- but the reason is NEW and must not be filed with the five EMPTY verdicts before it. Proposed sixth/seventh-sibling disposition name: NARROW-BAND-UNMEASURABLE. The domain was not shown to be empty; it was shown to be UNMEASURABLE from a frame corpus. No gate id was created.
axecull_preflight_20260822T1800Z.why_that_zero_decides_nothing: THE POINT OF THIS ROUND. Three in-ring enemy-frames against a 25-point window on a health pool of order 1000 gives an expected hit count near 0.08 even if the defect is entirely real. You would need ~40 in-ring frames to expect ONE hit and several hundred for a quotable rate. The fixture library is about two orders of magnitude too small to answer this question. Recording this as 'domain empty' -- the shape of the five previous pre-flights -- would have been a false negative dressed as rigour.

axet20_20260827.t20_why: [5] pays in attack damage and health, both currencies this Axe is already long on or cannot use: no Consider* in the file has a right-click decision layer (all four are Q/W/E/R), neither role list buys attack speed or a damage item, so +15 attack damage compounds with nothing and is under 9 dps at a 1.7 base attack time; the health half lands on the hero whose pos_3 list opens item_tank_outfit -> item_crimson_guard -> item_blade_mail, the one axis the build already spends its first ~8.5k on. [6] pays in PURE damage, which neither this build nor the enemy's supplies: armor does not touch it, t20 unlocks in the last third of a turbo game (exactly when the mode's fast timings have bought enemy cores the armor [5]'s physical half runs into), it is 160 -> 200 at the rank held there (+25% on the hero's principal damage source), and it is the only damage he has that multiplies by the number of enemies present -- the state X.ConsiderQ manufactures on purpose.
axet20_20260827.t20_why_affordable: hero_axe.lua has NO talent5 and NO talent6 handle, so the flip is inert to the decision layer and can only move combat power -- it cannot create a stale read in either direction. [8] (+150 Culling Blade damage) would be bought and then not used: the kill-check is a hardcoded 150 + 100*lv so no fold reaches it, and the talent term beside it reads 0 (GH #228). campdanger_20260826.defect: bots/mode_farm_generic.lua Think() negated a call to a J.Site field named IsCampDangerous. The name is declared in no file under bots/ under any of the six declaration forms, and J.Site is require(FunLib/aba_site), a transpiled module of plain `____exports.name = function` assignments with no setmetatable and no __index -- so no dynamic fall-back exists and the field is nil. The line raised `attempt to call a nil value` INSIDE Think(). The engine's error handler is broken and print() never reaches the console, so it never read as a crash: it read as a SILENT Think abort, UNGATED, in every game, on every frame where a farming bot's nearest available camp was >200u closer than its current pick. Everything below that point in Think() -- the entire preferedCamp block that walks to the camp and attacks the neutrals -- was eaten on those frames.
campdanger_20260826.fix: Split at the line where the evidence stops being forced. UNGATED half (forced): the nil call is gone; the conjunct now reads `X.IsCampSwitchSafe(nearest)`, a real local predicate that returns false unarmed. False is byte-for-byte the camp decision the abort produced -- an abort updates nothing, so 'no switch' IS the shipped verdict -- and the only unarmed change is that Think() runs on, which is the tail the abort was eating. GATED half ('campdanger', turbo-only): armed, the predicate answers the question the conjunct asks -- switch to the nearer camp unless an enemy hero was last seen within 800u of it.

cap25_boundary_20260825.boundary_rule: ⚠️ READINGS TAKEN ON EITHER SIDE OF THIS COMMIT ARE NOT COMPARABLE, and the reason is not only game length. cmboots_RESOLVE_20260825T2130Z.condition_c: NOT SATISFIED AS FILED, on four legs. (1) THE RULE'S OWN TEST RETURNS THE OPPOSITE FOR THIS HERO. Iron rule 2(c) names web-retrievable standard strategy as the corroboration method. Retrieved 2026-08-25: the standard boot for Crystal Maiden is Tranquil Boots, and the reason given is Arcane Aura plus Tranquil's own regen, i.e. exactly the claim the request needs to establish ('CM has no mana item, therefore she should buy one') has already been considered and rejected in standard play FOR THIS HERO SPECIFICALLY. (2) THE OBVIOUS REBUTTAL WAS CHECKED BY THE DIRECTOR AND DOES NOT HOLD. The rebuttal available to the hero desk is that the aura is weak across the scored window: tests/mock/special_value_shapes.lua:293 gives base_mana_regen 0.4/0.6/0.8/1 and proximity_bonus_factor 3 => 1.2 mana/s in-radius at rank 1, and hero_crystal_maiden.lua:19's level-up queue {1,2,3,2,2,6,2,1,1,1,6,3,3,3,6} puts the aura's second point at hero level 12, so the batch's 10-min-capped window is scored at 40% aura. TRUE BUT NON-DISTINGUISHING: the human standard build also holds Arcane Aura at one point until late and still chooses Tranquil, so this fact is already priced into the advice in (1). It does not separate bot from human and therefore cannot rescue (c). (3) THE ONE GENUINELY BOT-SPECIFIC MEASUREMENT POINTS UPSTREAM, NOT AT THE BOOTS. The request measured, but did not draw the conclusion from, this: teammates cast Replenish 2.8-4.4 times per game while CM RECEIVES 0.00-1.07 (1200 radius); frame example 1d9ae5/033503_slot9 has lina and zuus casting 11 times and CM receiving 0. The same 1200 is Arcane Aura's proximity_bonus_radius. So one positioning pathology is simultaneously eating her own aura's 3x proximity bonus AND the team's Replenish. 'CM has no mana item' is the symptom; 'CM stands outside the team's mana radius' is the cause, and the cause is free to move while the boots cost 375g. (4) THE LEDGER IS NOT NEUTRAL, IT IS NEUTRAL-WITH-A-COST. Bought: +2.04 casts/game, mp<100 -3.5pp (read as a floor -- offline there is no per-ability mana table and 100 is below every CM ability). Sold: boots completion median +70~85s (394-420s vs 313-344s, both layers same sign) and ancient_janggo completion -21.9pp (both layers same sign, -17/-27); janggo is entry 2 of the pos_5 list, i.e. the item immediately behind the boots, so this is the whole downstream list sliding. Deaths two layers opposite sign => not read (iron rule 4(i)). And on the win side, +7.03 gpm sits INSIDE this same wave's own structural null leg (|-5.41| gpm, seed 888) => (b) bought 'no clear negative', it did not buy 'this helps'. The purpose of the owner's three-condition rule is to spare well-grounded harmless changes from significance testing; it is not a route by which a change whose stated grounding retrieves backwards, and whose ledger carries a two-layer same-sign cost, ships on 'it did not get worse'.

cmqreach_20260830.axis: REACH -- a point the file computed against a bound WIDER than the bound it may cast into. New axis; the previous four triggers (zusstatic / odbuild / wkt25 / lionqdmg) all asked what a NUMBER was worth. This one asks whether a computed LOCATION is one the hero is allowed to use.
cmqreach_20260830.bug: Thirteen `return DESIRE, <result>.targetloc` sites consume those searches and X.SkillsComplement feeds whatever comes back straight into bot:ActionQueue_UseAbilityOnLocation( abilityQ, castQLoc ). Split by the search that filled them: HERO 5 sites, all contained -- 4 re-check GetUnitToLocationDistance(bot, loc) against nCastRange (one at +50) and the 5th reads a separate search run at nCastRange - 300. CREEP 8 sites, ZERO checked. So the creep branches can hand the dispatch chain a cast location up to nRadius = 425 units past the cast range: the overshoot is 58.06% of the whole cast range, and it is invariant in rank, level and items (Aether Lens adds 250 to both terms and cancels).
cmqreach_20260830.cost_NOT_claimed: DELIBERATELY UNCLAIMED, and this is the honest half. Whether the engine refuses an out-of-range location order or walks her into range first is NOT readable from the bot VM (AGENTS.md: print() never reaches the server console and the error handler is broken). Both readings are bad in different ways -- refusal means the creep branch wins the desire contest and does nothing, tick after tick, whenever a wave is out there; a walk means a position-5 support strolls up to 425 units into the enemy creep wave to farm. The argument for the fix is NOT a guess about which: it is that the hero branches in this very function refuse to do either, and the creep branches differ from them by one argument and eight missing checks. Domain reading requested in queue.json:hero-25.

The returned point is then in range BY CONSTRUCTION, exactly the way the 5th hero site already is: no new predicate, no new guard to get wrong. THE COST IS STATED, NOT HIDDEN: a 732 search cannot see more creeps than a 1157 one, so every `count >= 2/3/4/5` threshold is weakly harder and the armed side casts Nova on waves STRICTLY no more often than shipped. It never relocates a cast that was already legal.

crashguard_gate_ruling_20260831.ruling: ABORT-CONTAINED or it is not exempt. A repair ships ungated iff its behavioral difference from the shipped code is contained in the set of frames where the shipped code RAISES. Two source-checkable halves: (a) on every frame the fallback does NOT fire, the new code evaluates the same expressions verbatim as the old (the same 'off path reproduces factory output verbatim' check used for admission); (b) the fallback's trigger condition is a SUBSET of the old code's raise condition, never a superset. Half (b) is the entire cutting edge: `X == nil` IS the raise condition of `X.f` and qualifies; `X.count == nil` is the raise condition of nothing, so a guard written on it is a behavior change wearing a crash guard's clothes and goes through gated-fix.
crashguard_gate_ruling_20260831.scope_limit: THE EXEMPTION IS ABOUT THE DIFFERENCE SET, NOT ABOUT EFFICACY. Silencer and CM each still leave three sibling FindAoELocation results indexed unguarded in the same function (350 of the repo's 353 sites are unguarded). Those repairs therefore SHRINK the raise set without emptying it -- and that does not touch the exemption, because an incomplete crash guard is still abort-contained. Merging the two questions yields 'incomplete => must gate', i.e. 'because it is not thorough enough, keep crashing'. Completeness is an issue; gating is a difference set. Also: CR.2 is an exemption CONDITION, not a licence to go edit the other 350 sites.

crashguard_gate_ruling_20260831.why_not_gate: The load-bearing reason is NOT the hero desk's ('gating means keep crashing'), though that holds. It is: A GATE WHOSE CONDITION (a) IS UNBUYABLE BY CONSTRUCTION IS NOT A GATE, IT IS A REJECTION. A gate defers pending evidence; for a crash guard the evidence has no channel in this repo -- print() never reaches the console, `error in error handling` eats the text (AGENTS.md), and the dumper samples world state at 1Hz with no 'Think raised this frame' term, so 'Think raised then did nothing' and 'Think decided to do nothing' are OBSERVATIONALLY IDENTICAL on the only instrument we own. Gating therefore permanently preserves a known crash while the ledger reads 'cautious'. It would mint a born-stuck id (pullcad / GH #326 family). Note the ruling needs NO engine fact: containment holds in BOTH worlds (never returns nil => the repair is a no-op; returned nil once => the differential is the raising frame). creepthink_20260830.defect: The creep-pull DRAG is structurally unreachable, not merely rare. mode_roam_generic.lua's creep-pull cadence is one if/elseif/else and ALL THREE arms sit behind Think()'s opening throttle `J.Utils.IsBotThinkingMeaningfulAction(bot, Customize.ThinkLess, "roam")`, whose list opens with ACTIVITY_RUN and ACTIVITY_ATTACK. A hero that just right-clicked its lane opponent is in ACTIVITY_ATTACK by construction for its whole attack cycle. Write R for the interval at which the throttle reopens; the cadence is evaluated only on reopened frames, where the time since the last poke is already >= R. So R > nBeat implies the `if` (POKE) is true on EVERY frame the cadence is reached, and the `else` (DRAG) is reached on NONE. Shipped nBeat is 1.2s and an early-game attack cycle is ~1.4-1.7s, so the shipped configuration sits on the wrong side of the inequality and the wave is never walked back -- the hero stands in the aggro it drew.
creepthink_20260830.evidence: GH #326's own bearing frame, read the other way: 20260830_003408_slot1 (seed 1828, ab/armed, W27) necrolyte -> jakiro inside a pull-certified episode -- SIX consecutive seconds of byte-identical coordinates (-5847,5064) while four melee lane creeps take it from 0.96 HP to 0.37, with four right-clicks at 252.4/254.0/255.4/257.0, gaps 1.6/1.4/1.6. That is the GH #186 zuus camp frame with lane creeps swapped in.

defclose_20260820.defect: aba_defend.GetClosestAllyPos(tPosList, vLocation) -- the arbiter for every 'only the nearest teammate of these roles may defend this building' rule -- scans the role list as if it were 1-based. The TS source walks j = 1..length reading tPosList[j] (0-based array), which tstl renders as tPosList[j+1] in the Lua, i.e. indices 2..#+1. The FIRST role in every list is never compared, index #+1 is nil, and `bestPos or tPosList[1]` falls back to precisely the never-compared role. So {4,5} can only ever answer 5 at ANY distance (or 4, also at any distance, when no role-5 hero is alive); {2,3} can only answer 3, fallback 2; {2,3,4,5} can never answer 2 -- which means ShouldDefend's under-fire gate disqualifies the mid outright, on top of role 1 which is not in the list at all. The distance test the function exists for is inert for the first role of every list; the tie-break degenerates to role number.

Both sides are the SAME query, jmz.GetLastSeenEnemiesNearLoc(botLocation, 1600). `pathEnemies` is that query bucketed to 500ms on the bot handle; `ds.nInRangeEnemy` is that query written at the BOTTOM of GetDefendDesireHelper, below SEVEN early returns -- one of which (`#closeEnemiesDefend > 0 and #closeAlliesDefend >= #closeEnemiesDefend`) fires on exactly the frames DefendThink runs on, i.e. whenever a fight is happening within 900. bot._defend is never reset, so during a fight the right-hand side freezes at its pre-fight value, or at the initial empty table (0) if no call ever reached the bottom. The comparison is therefore bought entirely by staleness, never by a real path/range difference -- and when true the bot walks 700 back toward its fountain and returns, abandoning every other DefendThink branch for the frame.

gh312_REPORT_NAME_RULING_20260830.finding: citation_audit.py's cadence leg parses a stream's rhythm off report filenames and folded every unparseable name into one aggregate `skipped` count. gh312_REPORT_NAME_RULING_20260830.fix: (A) of the three cures the issue offered. Malformed names are now classed apart (a `.md` whose name OPENS with a YYYYmmddT stamp is CLAIMING to be a report), counted separately, and printed one per line as `SKIPPED-IN-STREAM <stream>/<name>` with the interval its stamp could denote. Any cadence GAP that CONTAINS such a file carries `[!] ... likely a real work unit; fix the NAME, do not read this gap as idle`. The gap is still a finding -- an unfilled timestamp is a real defect -- so the fix corrects the READING without muting the leg. The recovered stamp is an INTERVAL parsed from the name (`10xx` -> the whole hour), never git's commit time: when a file landed is a different question from when the round ran.

hero2_BANDPOWER_20260830.finding: The `hero-2` lever (Axe's Culling Blade kill-check hardcodes 150 + 100*lv = 250/350/450 against a real 275/375/475) has been blocked since 2026-08-22 by ONE published power calculation, and that calculation prices the wrong population. tests/test_axe_culling_threshold_preflight.lua concluded NARROW-BAND-UNMEASURABLE from `3 in-ring enemy-frames against a 25-point window on a health pool of order 1000 gives an expected count near 0.08 ... you would need roughly 40 in-ring frames`, and generalised it to `a lever whose domain is a narrow BAND on a continuous quantity cannot be sized from a frame corpus at all -- size it on the EVENT side, or not at all`. That is the POOL model: it prices the band as band/health_pool, i.e. it asks how often a UNIFORMLY DRAWN enemy-frame lands in the window. An enemy never occupies the band uniformly -- it ENTERS from above on its way down, so the question is whether a sample lands during the traverse. At sampling period dt and health velocity v the time in band is band/v, so a crossing is caught with p = min(1, band/(v*dt)) -- a quantity that contains no health pool term at all.
hero2_BANDPOWER_20260830.limits: (i) The crossing model assumes a monotone descent at roughly constant velocity and a sampling phase independent of the crossing; heal, regen and a burst that overshoots the whole band in one tick all break it in the SAME direction (fewer catches), so the numbers are an UPPER bound on capture -- read them as `at least this many crossings`, never `this many suffice`. (ii) `observed.burst` is damage dealt TO the fixture's subject BY enemy heroes; using it as the velocity of a target being killed assumes hero-on-hero damage rates are symmetric in distribution -- it is the corpus's own measurement of the right physical quantity on the wrong end of the fight. (iii) Fixtures with an all-zero burst (49 of 107) are excluded: a hero taking no damage is not crossing anything, so the median is conditioned on `a fight is happening`. (iv) Rings ignore vision, exactly as the preflight's did, so they are UPPER bounds on what the engine's list would show -- safe direction for a `the corpus cannot settle this` claim. (v) All 22 ready frames are rank 1 or 2; rank 3, where the band is (450, 475] and hero_axe.lua's t25 talent note lives, is untested at every level. (vi) Nothing here is a frequency estimate.

M1/M2 reddening 7 and 5 cases is BY DESIGN and is recorded rather than trimmed: the band width is a shared input to every case that prices it, so a band that is zero or negative must invalidate every model built on it. illureal_20260901.main_criterion: WHEN A PREDICATE ABOUT THE WORLD IS STORED AS A HAND-MAINTAINED FIELD, ITS TRUTH STOPS BEING A FACT ABOUT THE WORLD AND BECOMES A FACT ABOUT WHETHER EVERY WRITER REMEMBERED. The predicate is then only as reachable as its least diligent caller, and it fails in the OFF direction and in SILENCE: an unset field is indistinguishable from an honest `false`, so the guarded branch simply never happens -- nothing errors, no counter moves, and no test can tell 'this unit is not an illusion' from 'nobody flagged this illusion'. The tell is countable and needs no frame: ONE predicate with TWO live spellings in the same file (a field and the engine call answering the same question), with different branches reading different ones. Where that happens, count the WRITERS of the field against the CALLERS of the branch. Here it is 2 against 127. Distinguish from the five same-family findings before it: GH #348 ORDER, GH #368 LEXICAL SCOPE, GH #370 UNREPORTED SIDE EFFECT, GH #373 LATCH RECORDING THE ATTEMPT, GH #378 THROTTLE SCOPE. l1xpsoak_DISPOSITION_20260819.reason: Condition (a) is structurally unprovable in the current design, not merely unproven. The single consumption point (mode_retreat_generic) discards the Vector that ShouldXpSoakLane returns -- the absolute anchor that was the whole point of the 20260819 redesign -- and only tests it for nil, then returns the same BOT_MODE_DESIRE_HIGH as lanesurv. Its entry condition is a strict subset of lanesurv's (1200/>=2 enemies vs 1100/>=1, same 3.0s window, same HP*0.75 threshold), so of 335 entry episodes across 12 games, 97.3% are judged identically by the already-promoted lanesurv; the 9 exclusive frames (2.7%) showed no attributable behavioral difference under frame-by-frame review. More games cannot fix this -- the bottleneck is mechanism indistinguishability, not sample size.

l1xpsoak_MECHANISM_20260731: A1 mechanism analysis (123 mirror games + 6 frame-by-frame): the solo -50 is MOSTLY the last remaining laning-Think replacement wiring -- zero-trigger heroes (storm 0s soak time, 0/7 vs mirror 1/0) were the biggest losers via the condemned c3 CS body; the CS deficit (-3.8 lh, -30pct denies) alone explains the gpm gap. The rule itself also kills when it DOES fire: panic bar too late (75pct burst = death already adjacent), relative anchor 'walk 420u fountain-ward' = death march (medusa chased 17s, tp_cd=0 unused, 6 deaths in 8 zoned entries), boundary oscillation walks full-HP heroes BACK past the midline, lvl1-3 exemptionless bar fires on normal 1v2 opens. Owner's artifact intuition CONFIRMED in direction, wrong source: the artifact was OUR wiring, not soft opponents (opponents punished hard). FIXES LANDED: bXpSoak unwired from laning Think (last takeover id gone), panic rehomed to RETREAT desire (can TP/escape), early exemption (t<90s or HP>85pct never fires). Deferred to redesign: absolute anchor posture, exit hysteresis. Analyst predicts solo reading converges to +-10 after the unwiring (step-0 verification when next tested)

lanehyst_20260819.anti_parking_brake: TIME-BOUNDED on purpose, unlike the l1xpsoak hold (which released only on state change and could hold indefinitely). 2.0s can smooth a blink; it cannot become the force-passivity failure mode that rejected lf_recover / corefarm / l1xpsoak wave 1.
lanehyst_20260819.change: J.ShouldRetreatLaneBurst (jmz_func.lua): on a true frame it stamps bot.laneBurstLastFire = DotaTime(); when the base bar is missed and 'lanehyst' is armed, it keeps returning true for up to J.nLaneBurstHysteresisWindow = 2.0s past that stamp, provided no peel-capable ally arrived and incoming is still >= J.nLaneBurstHysteresisFloor = 0.40 of current HP. Every enemy leaving 1100 releases earlier still (existing early-out). Off the gate the stamp is written but never read -> shipped decision unchanged.
lanehyst_20260819.decision: Took the SECOND path, with one refinement: the hysteresis lands GATED behind a NEW id 'lanehyst' rather than as an edit to the promoted default. Folding it straight into lanesurv would silently change shipped turbo behavior for every bot with no way to A/B it; a new gate keeps the shipped decision byte-identical and makes the change measurable on its own.
lanehyst_20260819.rationale_c: Schmitt trigger on a blinking binary control signal. GetEstimatedDamageToTarget is mana/cooldown-aware, so a nuke coming off cooldown / an enemy stepping 20u past 1100 / a mana tick flips the decision between adjacent frames; a retreat that wins the desire auction for one frame and loses it the next issues a move order and cancels it -- neither retreating nor laning. The codebase already applies the same medicine on the l1kite path (bot.laneKiteUntil kite-lock, added for watched 181046 CK flapping).

lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.coverage_gap_it_closed: GH #31 sec.4 was right about the root cause of survival: tests/test_l1_trade.lua and tests/test_l5_combo.lua only ever asserted the TRIGGER (J.Should*), and tests/test_divecap_gate.lua only the cap predicate in isolation. Nothing asserted their COMPOSITION -- the number the engine actually receives. That composition is now covered. Any future branch in this file whose comment reasons about a relative desire ordering should get the same end-to-end assertion.
lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.defect: bots/mode_team_roam_generic.lua: the L1-TRADE and L5-COMBO branches bid RemapValClamped(hp,0,0.5,NONE,0.92) -- 0.92 chosen explicitly to outbid the PROMOTED lanesurv retreat at BOT_MODE_DESIRE_HIGH=0.75. But GetDesire() pipes the helper's value through CapForLanePush, which soft-ceils any desire >0.9 to 0.72 whenever J.IsInLaningPhase() or J.IsPushing(). Both J.ShouldInitiateLaneKill and J.ShouldSupportComboKill HARD-REQUIRE J.IsInLaningPhase(), so the cap's trigger condition is a strict SUPERSET of the two branches' entire domain: the 0.92 literal was unreachable on every frame they could possibly fire, the effective bid (0.72) landed BELOW the 0.75 it was picked to beat, and the effective bid was NON-MONOTONIC in HP (healthy core 0.72, half-HP core ~0.90). Neither branch set bDefensiveCollapse, and the existing 'divecap' exemption is both collapse-only and itself unarmed.
lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.fix: New frame flag bLaneKillCommit (mirrors the existing bDefensiveCollapse pattern), reset each frame in GetDesireHelper, raised inside the two lane-kill branches, and exempted in _divecap_CapForLanePush (4th param). No extra soak gate on the exemption: the flag is only reachable from inside branches already gated on 'l1trade'/'l5combo'. Cap behavior for every other path is byte-identical. The 0.92 literal was KEPT (not lowered to <=0.9): bidding just under a cap threshold is the same implicit coupling that produced this bug.
lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.risk_accepted: Uncapping restores the designed 0.92 > lanesurv 0.75 ordering, i.e. 'initiate beats retreat'. The wave13 20260723 failure mode (a 0.95 bid pinning bots into losing trades) is guarded by J.ShouldReleaseLaneCommit (self-release when the committing bot is the one dying) plus the once-per-engagement 4s commit lock, both already present and both required by the new source-level test. Both ids stay gated, so this rides as a test-set candidate, not a shipped default.
lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.same_family_as: GH #29 (retreat guard chain priority inversion). Both are 'the desire the author wrote is not the desire the engine sees' -- an author-intended relative ordering silently destroyed by a downstream transform. Worth treating as a recurring class, not two incidents.
lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.shipped_default_impact: NONE. Both raise sites sit inside branches whose helpers return nil unless turbo AND the soak candidate is armed, so with all gates off the flag is never raised and CapForLanePush is unchanged. Pinned by a source-level containment test, not just by inspection.

MUTATION-CHECKED twice: deleting the exemption (byte-equivalent to the pre-fix source) fails 4 tests including both end-to-end ones reporting the 0.72 clobber; deleting one raise site fails exactly the 2 relevant tests. lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.why_no_real_frame_fixture: The two helpers' decisive gates (lethality: combined castable burst >= target HP + 4s regen; self-risk: their burst vs mine) both run GetEstimatedDamageToTarget, which the behav dumper does not record (GH #27, GH #28 both flag the same gap). So no archived frame can be replayed into a state where the trigger provably returns non-nil -- a fixture could pin the geometry but not the firing. The defect is also a domain-wide arithmetic fact (cap domain superset of branch domain), which a single frame cannot express: the monotonicity sweep is the honest form of that claim.

lion_t15_no_flip_20260823T0600Z.deciding_channel: Scarcity. A cooldown reduction only pays when the cooldown is what stopped a cast. The <= 2s conversion band is hit on 0 of the 11 on-cooldown frames against an expectation of ~0.9 => UNDERPOWERED, not EMPTY (GH #115).

liondrain_20260819.root_cause: The two COMBAT drain branches in X.ConsiderE (团战吸蓝 / 打架抽蓝) sit below `if X.IsOtherAbilityFullyCastable() or nSkillLV <= 1 then return 0 end`, so they only fire when Impale, Hex AND Finger are all unavailable -- exactly the state in which a support at melee range should be leaving. liondrainstop_20260820.prereg_for_batch_desk: Pre-registered expectation on the 5-game census: this guard adds RELEASES to channels that started clean and turned unsafe (an enemy walked into the danger radius during them). The FIRST-lever `liondrain` already refuses to START 4 of the 13 channels; the SECOND-lever `liondrainstop` targets a DIFFERENT class -- channels that pass the start check but face incoming pressure mid-channel. Condition (b) MUST be judged with BEHAVIORAL DETECTORS (channels released early / channels released for reasons other than IsRetreating / Lion HP-loss profile across a channel window), NOT gpm/xpm -- these are fewer than 1 event per game, structurally invisible in economy aggregates (GH #30 noise floor).
liondrainstop_20260820.problem: The shipped X.ConsiderStopDrain is the ONLY way to break a running Mana Drain channel (once it starts, X.SkillsComplement's `if J.CanNotUseAbility(bot) then return` early-out catches IsChanneling and everything else is unreachable). But that release only fires on `J.IsRetreating(bot)` -- and by construction a rooted hero is not walking home, so retreat mode does not kick in during a fight. Result: a channel that STARTS clean and turns unsafe (an enemy walks in / begins hitting Lion mid-channel) rides out its 5s while Lion stands still, taking damage. The FIRST lever `liondrain` only refuses to START unsafe channels; it cannot help a clean start that turned bad.
liondrainstop_20260820.root_cause: Same shape as cmrguard / cmrself and liondrain: a self-channeled ability with no self-preservation term on the release side. Shipped ConsiderStopDrain reads only J.IsRetreating; the mode is structurally unreachable inside the very state the release needs to break out of.

liondrainstop_20260820.why_new_id_not_liondrain: Separate levers: start-refusal fires BEFORE the channel begins, stop-release fires AFTER. They live in different Consider* functions and would be untestable jointly (the axeblink trap: two levers bundled where the second's precondition is masked by the first). Independent ids make bisect trivial.
liondrainstop_20260820.why_symmetric_predicate: The signal that decides `do not start` is the same signal that decides `stop what you started` -- if a hero is currently killing Lion inside the danger radius, roots are bad regardless of whether the root is 0.0s or 4.0s old. Deliberate symmetry: any retune of the danger radius must move both levers together, which is what the shared X.nEDrainDangerRadius constant guarantees.

liont25_20260827.why_2_bot_specific: The half that is ours. lion_voodoo is DOTA_ABILITY_BEHAVIOR_UNIT_TARGET, so the engine applies the +250 radius on cast: a bot collects the ENTIRE talent with zero aiming, zero prediction and zero new code. lion_impale is a LINE skillshot with travel time -- the one ability on this hero that must be led -- and [8] would raise its cast range 500 -> 1100, more than doubling the lead distance on the ability the bot is worst at. So the two talents are not merely unequal, they are unequal in the direction that MATTERS FOR A BOT: [7] is worth more to a bot than to a human and [8] is worth less.
liont25_20260827.why_3_structural_repair: It removes GH #166's defect BY CONSTRUCTION rather than gating around it. Fifteen reads in hero_lion.lua ask `talent8` whether Hex is an area spell, while slot 8 is the Earth-Spike-range half and does not touch lion_voodoo at all. A hero trains ONE talent per tier, so with the row on [7] `talent8` is structurally untrained, X.IsHexAoe answers false everywhere, and FALSE IS THE CORRECT ANSWER for a unit-target ability under either talent: the entity dispatch is kept and the cast-legality check is no longer skipped. Nothing is lost, because the engine applies the radius whether or not this file knows about it.

His t25 row is {10,0} = index [8] = special_bonus_unique_lion_2 (+600 Earth Spike cast range) -- exactly the half that makes every `talent8` read in hero_lion.lua answer TRUE while the code believes it means 'Hex is an area spell now' (GH #166; the Hex-radius talent is [7], the other half of the same row). lvlpremise_20260827.the_worry_that_turned_out_unfounded_and_: ability_item_usage_generic.lua consumes sSkillList strictly from the head and does NOT skip an entry it cannot level -- the only escape is guarded by `botLevel > 25`. So a talent queued before its tier would stall everything behind it. Driven out of the real J.Skill.GetSkillList: talents land at list positions 10, 15, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23. That reads wrong and is right, because a list position is the Nth ability point SPENT (which is how the consumer itself reads it: nPointsSpent = botLevel - bot:GetAbilityPoints()). 15 ability points plus one at each of 10/15/20/25 puts position 18 at level 20 and position 19 at level 25 exactly. Positions 20-23 are the other half of each already-taken tier, permanently unlevelable -- and never dequeued, because there is no 20th point. 'The tail is dead weight' is true; 'the tail jams the queue' is not, and they are different claims.
lvlpremise_20260827.what_corrected_means_here: NOT deleting the quote. The premise should stay quoted -- the verdicts written on top of it are unreadable without it (same shape as section 4 of test_focus_talent_anchor.lua: the stale ladder may be quoted, never used). A site counts as corrected when its own comment block names GH #235 or the 2026-08-27 correction within 14 lines. So the ratchet cannot be satisfied by censorship, only by writing down what replaced the claim; an anti-vacuum assertion (>= 9 quoted sites must survive in bots/) enforces that directly.

lvlpremise_20260827.world_assertion_registered_not_asserted: That a hero receives an ability point at levels 1-15 and at 10/15/20/25 and at no other level. midsupyield_20260823.safety: SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: the yield fires only when J.HasAvailableSupportResponder is true, i.e. a pos-4/5 teammate that is alive, level>=6, has a castable TP/BoT, and is not itself in a fight or retreating -- member-by-member the same gates the support would clear inside this helper. With no such support the core does NOT yield, so armed can only REALLOCATE a response to a support, never DROP one. Direction is also aligned with the known econ problem: it strictly REDUCES core off-farm TP participation (the residual-fingerprint defensive-gravity pull), never increases it.

midsupyield_20260823.what: Backlog #4 'suptp x midtp 协同仲裁' (owner, state.json keep_optimize/teambrain: 'suptp needed but must COORDINATE with midtp -- response arbitration'). J.ShouldTpSupportTowerFight is shared by 'midtp' (any position) and 'suptp' (pos 4/5); the only thing separating which one answers a tower fight is J.TryTakeTpResponseSlot, a position-BLIND module-level FCFS ledger (one gated responder per 6s). So on a frame where both a core (midtp) and a support (suptp) would go, whoever asks first burns the slot -- a race. New gated soak candidate 'midsupyield': when a CORE reaches the quota take and a viable SUPPORT responder exists, the core returns nil, ceding the slot. First concrete cut of the TeamBrain phase-1 response-arbitrator ('one event -> one best responder').

outlatch_20260831.main_criterion: A LATCH MUST RECORD THE POSTCONDITION IT GATES, NOT THE ATTEMPT. The flag's name asks 'did we GET'; the code answers 'did we LOOK'. Whenever a do-this-once flag is set on the way out of the block that was supposed to produce something, the empty result is indistinguishable from the full one -- permanently, because that flag is the only thing that would ever run the producer again. Distinguish from the three same-family findings: GH #348 is ORDER (a nil guard below the index it guards), GH #368 is SCOPE (a guard naming a different variable than the consumer), GH #370 is an UNREPORTED SIDE EFFECT (a callee that orders while reading like a query). Here producer, flag and consumer are each correct in isolation; the flag simply answers a different question than the consumer asks.
outlatch_20260831.method_self_harm: Extracting the function body with `function GetClosestOutpost%(%).-\nend` stops at the FIRST nested `end`, returning a TRUNCATED body; the read count came out one short and still matched a plausible expected number -- a scanner that returns less than it claims fails by AGREEING with you. It passed silently for one run. Fixed by slicing between the two neighbouring `function` headers. Same family as GH #341/#345 (a tool that never evaluates the clause it says it reads) and GH #370 (a source scan that counted its own comment).
outlatch_20260831.second_consequence_registered_not_fixed: GetClosestOutpost's conjunction evaluates `not Outposts[i]:IsNull()` FOURTH, after `Outposts[i]:GetTeam()` and `GetUnitToUnitDistance(bot, Outposts[i])` on the same handle. Lua's `and` is left-to-right short-circuit, so the guard whose whole job is 'this handle may have gone away' runs two method calls too late -- GH #348's shape in a second file. Its worth is a direct consequence of the latch above (the table is filled once and never refreshed). Pinned by [source S6], which asserts the defect is STILL PRESENT so that the day it moves the test file is re-derived rather than silently passing. NOT fixed this round -- one lever at a time.

pingstamp_WORLD_ASSERTION_14_20260821.two_structural_facts_pinned: (1) X.ShouldRun's `enemyFountainDistance < 1000` leg can NEVER reach the block on its trigger frame: same helper, same frame, disjoint intervals against the block's `> 2200`. (2) A fixture can only ever see the FIRST frame of a runMode episode. GetDesireHelper sets runMode when ShouldRun fires and holds it for `shouldRunTime` seconds WITHOUT RE-ASKING (the returned value doubles as the duration: 1.33 to 3.33s), and every fixture VM starts at runTime = 0. This is a THIRD kind of harness blindness, distinct from the twelfth (a datum the dump has and the loader drops) and the thirteenth (a datum the dump never had): here the state is reconstructible, but only at its onset. Therefore '5 frames out of 940' must NOT be read as the in-game frequency.

pollyhp_20260827.criterion: **主判据(本轮主产出,两条):(一)「这四处 getter 该统一到哪一侧」这个问题预设了 override 是一件事 —— 它是两件:一条哨兵(666)和一条建模(护盾)。哨兵在任何比较里都不是测量;建模只有在它建模的那个资源**就是本次动作作用的资源**时才是测量。所以「统一」不是一个原子,按**成分**拆。(二)同一个 consider 内部两处读数要的是**相反**的一侧**:门问「这次治疗能补回多少」(必须 Original,因为补的是血),选人问「谁最接近死」(护盾吸收是真的,建模值更对)。任何全文件统一都会在其中一处答错 —— 这是对 `0SALT`「轴是全文件一起定」的**限定**,不是推翻:轴按**问题**定,不按**文件**定。
pollyhp_20260827.defect: `X.ConsiderItemDesire["item_polliwog_charm"]` 的队友门 `allyHero:GetMaxHealth() - allyHero:GetHealth() > 100` 是本文件四处队友选择里**唯一**走 override 版 getter 的一处。`aba_global_overrides.lua` 把 `GetHealth` 换成了「不可见 ⇒ 常数 666」**加**「美杜莎 = 血 + 当前魔法能吸收的伤害(mana*2.6*0.95,12 级以下折半)」;`GetMaxHealth` 带同一项但走**最大**魔法。于是 override 下的「缺血量」= (缺血) + (缺魔)*k —— 而这枚装备补的是**血**。归档里这不是稀有情形而是**全部情形**:5 个(持有者, 1000 内活着的友方美杜莎)配对**5/5** 被出厂门放行、被 Original 对拒绝,而她们在 **98.7%–100.0%** 真实血量上,最大一笔幻影缺口 **497.9**(其中每一点都是魔法)。

pullbeat_20260823.defect: The cadence orders the aggro poke and then, on the VERY NEXT Think (1/30 s later), issues Action_MoveToLocation(pull.retreat) -- which cancels an attack whose wind-up has not started. Creep aggro only redirects once the attack BEGINS, so the pre-fix cadence draws aggro by luck. Driving the shipped Think on a real laning frame prints it literally: 'A' then 36 consecutive 'M', every beat, forever.

Everything else in the ShouldCreepPullLane chain passes on 73/966 frames (vetoes: 291 late, 177 no enemy in the ring, 142 out of laning phase, 123 support, 81 hurt, 76 second enemy, 3 recently damaged) -- a live, non-degenerate domain.

pullbeat_20260823.issue_recommendation_REJECTED: GH #143 asked for an END condition ('stop dragging ~2.5 s after the last attack'). That targets a mechanism this code does not have: bot.roamCreepPull is re-derived by GetDesire EVERY frame, and J.ShouldCreepPullLane requires an aggro target within 1000 AND enemy lane creeps within 900 on that same frame -- so the drag already self-terminates when the wave or the target leaves. The desk's own number agrees: longest run of consecutive pull frames = 2 across 5,105 episodes on BOTH legs. The long walks home it measured are not pull frames. Reported back on the issue.
pullbeat_20260823.known_gap: The 0.5 s is a literal, not GetAttackPoint(): slow-wind-up heroes (Lina 0.65) are still cancelled a little early, fast ones hold slightly long. pullthink_20260825.defect: bots/mode_roam_generic.lua's camp-pull cadence pokes the camp every 3.0s and walks 500u lane-ward on the frames in between. The walk is never ordered on the frames that matter, because Think() opens two lines above the cadence with `if J.Utils.IsBotThinkingMeaningfulAction(bot, Customize.ThinkLess, "roam") then return end`, and utils.lua's meaningfulActivities list opens with ACTIVITY_RUN and ACTIVITY_ATTACK. A hero mid-attack-animation on the camp it just poked is in ACTIVITY_ATTACK by construction, and the neutrals hitting back keep it there -- so the throttle returns on exactly the frames the drag has to be issued on. The camp branch is never reached; the hero stands in the camp and tanks it. That is the wave13 'stood and TANKED the neutrals' fingerprint the cadence was written to remove, coming back through a line the cadence cannot see.

reclaimblind_BOUND_RULING_20260830.a_ruling: W28 reads exit 0, and it now reads it FROM THE TOOL, not from this prose. Verified against the source, not the desk's summary: check_bracket is a self-consistency guard on the constant and is structurally disjoint from the BLINDED decision (low_yield and early_reclaims). On W28 paired_n=4 => low_yield False; zero RECLAIMED => early_reclaims empty; both conjuncts independently false => the decision branch returns 0. The desk's reasoning was correct and its refusal to self-clear was correct.
reclaimblind_BOUND_RULING_20260830.b_correction: The desk's cited coincidence -- W28 seed 1850 corrected to 42.58 vs 'historical shortest paired survivor 42.60 (W21 seed 995), 0.02 min apart' -- rests on a STALE number and should not be propagated. Directly from the wave records: W24 seed 1633 is a first-hand paired survivor (ab27/ba13, arm_depth 17.55, SIR 06:18:41Z->06:59:19Z) at 40.63 min. The measured bracket has been (34.8, 40.63], not (34.8, 42.6], since 2026-08-29 -- a day BEFORE W28 -- and nobody registered it because reclaim_blind.py's own history table stopped at W21. 40.0 still sits inside, so the constant holds, but the margin to the upper edge is 0.63 min, not 2.6. The next paired machine under 40.0 refutes it for real.
reclaimblind_BOUND_RULING_20260830.b_ruling: The changeover constant 40.0 does NOT need re-deriving on a new proxy, and it was never refuted. The BRACKET VIOLATED was an artifact of the ESTIMATOR's bound direction, not of the data: last-S3-upload is a LOWER BOUND on survival, and the clause that fired (paired and survival < T) is precisely the direction in which a lower bound produces false positives, while the other clause (survival > T) stays sound under a lower bound. This is decidable without the desk's +2.90 offset at all -- which is the stronger form of its own honest boundary #1 (do not carry a self-destruct offset onto the reclaimed side): the fix uses NO offset, so it cannot leak one.
reclaimblind_BOUND_RULING_20260830.c_ruling: LANDED. reclaim_blind is now a required key in wave.json:gates, absence = not run, enforced by tests/test_wave_gate_keys.py from W28 on (earlier records exempt -- the pending_rulings.py (甲) precedent: a check red from birth for historical reasons is a check people stop reading).
reclaimblind_BOUND_RULING_20260830.harness_fix: tools/batch_test/soak/reclaim_blind.py gains an optional per-machine `survival_bound` (exact|lower; absent = exact, so every pre-existing wave reads unchanged). On `lower`: the unsound 'moved earlier' bracket branch is SKIPPED OUT LOUD naming the machine (a check that quietly declines to run is the same lie as a gate that prints nothing); the sound 'moved later' branch stays armed; and the ATTRIBUTION clause becomes UNDECIDABLE (exit 2) for a reclaimed machine whose lower bound falls under the flip -- guessing 'before' invents a BLINDED and a 3x more expensive instrument, guessing 'after' hides one. An unnameable bound is exit 2, same stance as an unknown status_code. BRACKET_HI narrowed 42.6 -> 40.63 with its provenance; the printed bracket moved to 2dp and now states the margin, because at 1dp the upper edge read '40.6' against a 40.0 constant and rounded the entire remaining margin out of the only line that shows it.

residual_IS_A_CONSTANT_RULING_20260821T1.sigma: estimate moves to 18.36-19.94 (df=33); GH #30's 30.24 demoted to history (mechanism: it IS the l1xpsoak wave, tied-loudest in the archive, and was the sole 3-df data source). retnear_20260820.change: Armed, the count that may replace the nearby count is taken at 1600 (the same radius as the things it is compared with). The WIDE count is still computed and still feeds the 'nothing around at all' discount below (`nEnemyNearbyCount == 0 and unseenCount == 0`), which legitimately wants a wide horizon -- so exactly one lever moves. Armed can only lower or leave the retreat bid, never raise it. bots/mode_retreat_generic.lua only; no TS source for mode_* files.
retnear_20260820.defect: mode_retreat_generic.GetDesireHelper builds both hero lists at radius 1600 and asks J.WeAreStronger(bot, 1600) beside them, then OVERWRITES the enemy count with a last-seen count taken at radius 3200: `if unseenCount > #nEnemyHeroes then nEnemyNearbyCount = unseenCount end`. Both consumers underneath weigh that 3200-radius number against 1600-radius numbers -- `nEnemyNearbyCount - nAllyNearbyCount > 0` (+0.1875 per surplus) and `not bWeAreStronger and nEnemyNearbyCount >= nAllyNearbyCount` (+0.25). r=3200 is FOUR TIMES the area of r=1600, so the retreat bid leans 'outnumbered' as a matter of geometry: an ally standing 1700 away does not offset an enemy 3100 away, and 3200 is past the bot's own day vision (1800), so every enemy the wide count adds beyond that is one a TEAMMATE sees -- i.e. one that is near the teammate, not near the bot.
retnear_20260820.domain_measured: Six turbo replays (20260820_043120..043710), 43,256 hero-frames, each team's vision modelled from its own sources (heroes 1800, creeps 750, towers 1900, observers 1600 -- the .dem carries no fog bitmask, GH #27, so this is a MODEL and is reported as one): the wide count overwrites the near count on 7,908 frames (18.3%); the retreat bid differs on 6,556 (15.2% of all frames), modal delta 0.25 (4892), then 0.4375 (748), 0.1875 (736), 0.625 (102), >=0.8125 (29). Of 40 frames sampled from that set and driven through all 22 mode files, the auction winner changes on 4 (10%).

Distinct from GH #368 (scope) and GH #348 (ordering between branches): the caller here is not wrong about any value, it is missing a fact the callee never reported.

slotdust_20260902.instrument: TWO mock gaps had to be closed before this predicate could be evaluated on a frame AT ALL. (1) GetItemSlotType was UNSPECCED on fixture heroes. The first diagnosis this round wrote -- 'the ITEM_SLOT_TYPE_* constants were missing from _G' -- was WRONG and the mutation stand is what disproved it: api.install auto-resolves every unknown ALL_CAPS global to a distinct sentinel >= 1001, so the constants were never nil. The real mechanism is the getter: unspecced, `^Get` defaults to 0, so `GetItemSlotType(slot) == ITEM_SLOT_TYPE_MAIN` was `0 == 1174` -- FALSE on every frame in the corpus, every branch behind one constructively unreachable, failing CLOSED and silently. Same trap tests/test_fieldbuy_backpack_rescuer.lua:50 documents at a sibling site (GH #89's thirteenth world assertion). The repair is therefore the getter alone, off the dump's real 0-5 active / 6-8 backpack layout; the constants are deliberately NOT pinned to 0/1/2, because pinning MAIN to 0 would make every unit the loader does not build as a fixture hero report 'main inventory' by default -- turning a silent fail-closed into a silent fail-OPEN. [decision D3] asserts non-nil, mutually distinct AND non-zero so that stays true. (2) THE FIXTURE ITEM NAMESPACE IS NOT THE ENGINE ONE: the dumper writes snakeFromClass(GetClassName(), 'CDOTA_Item_') -- an ENTITY CLASS name -- and replay_fixture prefixed it with 'item_' as if it were the name FindItemSlot takes. Where the two spellings differ, every inventory predicate in bots/ that names the item finds NOTHING on every fixture and the test reads as a clean pass. Dust is the case this fix needed (class CDOTA_Item_DustofAppearance -- hence the twelve `modifier_item_dustofappearance` uses in bots/ -- but item `item_dust`, which item_purchase_generic.lua buys). Talents come in two families and only one owns a `value`: GENERIC talents (special_bonus_hp_200, special_bonus_strength_15) are real ability blocks in npc_abilities.txt, each carrying exactly one AbilityValues entry named `value`; HERO-UNIQUE talents (special_bonus_unique_axe_2) have NO KV block anywhere -- not in npc_abilities.txt, not in the hero's own npc_dota_hero_<h>.txt. talentvalue_20260826.the_expensive_lesson: A 'this string must not appear' assertion is unusable in a file that DISCUSSES the string. The first draft of the Zeus ratchet was find('bonus_arc_damage') == nil and it went red on the very correction it exists to protect -- retracting a wrong key means quoting it. Rewritten as an IMPLICATION (the mention is allowed; unretracted is not) and driven both ways. This is the exact dual of GH #214's lesson that 'this string must appear' is near-vacuous in a self-describing file: same family, opposite sign. Second-order: the retraction marker first spanned a comment line wrap, so a multi-word marker matched nothing -- an assertion aimed at prose must be aimed at prose that is contiguous.
talentvalue_20260826.the_load_bearing_reading: The dead term is dead in the SAFE direction, and the obvious repair is the regression. The KV shape (`"radius" { "value" "315"  "special_bonus_unique_axe_2" "+85" }`) exists so the engine can fold +85 into `radius` for a caster who trained the talent; there is nowhere else the bonus could live, so if the engine did not fold it the talent would do nothing in the game at all. Hence abilityQ:GetSpecialValueInt('radius') ALREADY carries the bonus and repointing the term at a handle that answered would DOUBLE-COUNT. This tree has already bet on that fold in a LANDED repair: GH #162's lionsplash reads lion_finger_of_death/splash_radius, which special_value_shape_census.py classifies NO-BASE -- no base value, only special_bonus_scepter "325". That read is worth something only if the engine resolves special_bonus_* sub-entries per caster. The 21 sites encode the opposite bet. Both cannot be right, and the KV shape says which is.
talentvalue_20260826.the_one_site_where_harmless_does_not_fol: A fold only reaches a number that was READ OFF THE ABILITY. hero_axe.lua's Culling Blade kill-check HARDCODES its base (nKillDamage = 150 + 100*nSkillLV), so no fold reaches it: that check is short the +150 talent as well as short the 25/level the already-registered hero-2 lever documents (KV damage is 275/375/475, the constant says 250/350/450). Both are collected by the SAME repair -- read the base off abilityR:GetSpecialValueInt('damage') -- which is hero-2, deliberately not taken here because it ADDS a cast. Annotated with the instruction that whoever takes hero-2 must drop the talent term in the same change, or the fold and the term double-count.
talentvalue_20260826.the_ratchet_key: The anchor keys sites on (file, var, slot) and NOT on the line number, because a line-number key is GH #221 verbatim -- three compliant commits knocked five pins off their rows in one day, every one of them having MOVED the code rather than broken it, and this change's own four annotations would have moved all four focus rows. The cost of dropping the line is that two reads on the same handle in one file share a key, and a plain SET comparison then answers green when a second read is added beside an existing one -- the direction that matters, a fresh silent zero shipping unremarked. Measured, not feared: that mutation escaped the set version on the first run. Compared as a MULTISET now.
talentvalue_20260826.the_second_lesson: The tool's own fixture caught a real bug in the tool. parse_talent_blocks sliced talent-start to talent-start, which looks equivalent while the talent blocks are contiguous and silently swallows the next ability's body the moment they are not -- reading `value` off a NEIGHBOUR and reporting a talent that declares nothing as answering. In the live file the LAST talent block absorbed the entire remainder of npc_abilities.txt unconditionally. Boundaries are now every one-tab block, filtered afterwards. It surfaced only because a fixture was added to close an escaped mutation -- the mutation drive paid for itself in a defect, not just in coverage.

RULING_for_the_weekly_ledger: PRIMARY comparable = output_tokens. Uniform price, and it tracks work actually produced.

SECONDARY = a cost-weighted input built from the components the script ALREADY prints separately (input_tokens uncached / cache_read_input_tokens / cache_creation_input_tokens), weighted by the current published rates at ledger time. Do not hardcode the weights into the script -- rates change and a stale constant would silently corrupt every future ledger.
NEVER rank groups on total_in. Quote it if you like, but label it 'billed input, cache-read dominated, not cost-proportional'.

Report model turns as model turns. A group whose count is inflated by subagents is not thereby less efficient -- check whether the transcripts include subagents before drawing any conclusion from that column.

token_ledger_CALIBRE_RULING_20260822T11x.no_code_change_needed: The script already prints all three input components on separate lines, so the ledger can compute the cost-weighted figure with no edit to tools/agent/token_usage.py. Left untouched deliberately.
token_ledger_CALIBRE_RULING_20260822T11x.total_in_is_NOT_cost_proportional: STAR. billed_in = input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens, summed 1:1. Cache reads are billed at a small fraction of base input and cache writes at a premium, so a 1:1 sum is dominated by cache_read and therefore measures WHOSE CONTEXT WAS LONGEST, not who did the most work. Ranking the groups on total_in would systematically penalise whichever group carries the biggest charter/corpus in context -- which is a property of the job, not of efficiency. That is exactly the wrong incentive for a ledger meant to catch idling and duplicated labour.
token_ledger_CALIBRE_RULING_20260822T11x.turns_means: Every JSONL record carrying message.usage, i.e. every ASSISTANT API RESPONSE (the script's own stdout calls it model_turns), summed across ALL transcripts under ~/.claude/projects -- main session PLUS every subagent it spawned. It is not conversation rounds and never was. In ledger prose call it 'model turns'.

tormself_20260901.main_criterion: A PREDICATE WHOSE DOMAIN IS ANOTHER UNIT, FED `self`, IS A TYPE ERROR THAT NEITHER THE LANGUAGE NOR THE RUNTIME CAN REPORT. `bot` and `botTarget` are the same duck type (a unit handle) and the predicate is TOTAL: on self it does not raise, it answers false, forever. The failure direction is OFF, and it is silent in the strongest sense available anywhere in this archive: there is no frame, no game and no replay on which the wrong answer DIFFERS from a correct `false`, because the correct answer for `self` IS false. Only the CALL SITE knows the question was meant for somebody else. The tell is countable and needs no frame: enumerate an identity predicate's call sites and look at what each is FED -- 227 of the 249 live J.IsTormentor call sites pass `botTarget` (90.8%), the rest pass some other unit handle, and EXACTLY ONE passes `bot` -- that one is the bug. Sharper: self-fed alone is NOT the rule, because J.IsMeepoClone(bot) is legitimately self-fed (a Meepo bot really can be a clone). The rule is SELF-FED AND UNSATISFIABLE-BY-SELF. Distinguish from the family: GH #348 is a MISSPELLING (an identifier that does not exist); #368 is LEXICAL SCOPE (right name, wrong binding); #370 is an UNREPORTED SIDE EFFECT; #373 is a latch recording the ATTEMPT not the POSTCONDITION; #378 is a throttle whose SCOPE exceeds what it throttles; #381 is a hand-maintained FIELD duplicating an engine fact. Here every identifier exists, is spelled right, is in scope, holds no state and is never stale, and the function called is the right function. The defect is entirely in WHICH OBJECT it is asked about.

tparrive_20260819.defect: J.ShouldTpSupportTowerFight's winnability gate is structurally blind to the responder it is deciding for. The helper requires the responder be > 3500 from the threatened tower and picks its target from the enemies within 1200 of that tower; J.SafeToCommitFight scores only heroes within 1200 of that target. The responder is therefore at least 2300 units outside its own read (asserted on all three acceptance frames), so 'is this collapse winnable' is evaluated as though the TP never happens -- it actually asks 'is this fight already fine WITHOUT me'. The helper's own HEAT GATE makes the inversion systematic: the ally the count is sure to include is REQUIRED to be hurt or under hero fire. Net effect: the 1-ally-dived-by-2 collapse the fix exists for is refused (1 >= 2 false), while the 2v2 that needs nobody is allowed. Same family as GH #29/#31/#32/#34/#35/#37 (test_set.md 0b: the helper's reasoning quietly invalidated by the consumed mechanism), and it is the FIRST case where the invalidating mechanism is the CALLER'S OWN precondition rather than a downstream transform.

tparrive_20260819.rationale_c: (1) A defensive TP under one's own tower to even a dive is textbook Dota -- the defender also gets tower damage and its own creep wave, so parity-on-arrival understates rather than overstates the defenders' side. Here the same branch omits a full-HP fighter that is definitely arriving. (3) The helper's own comment states the intent this restores: 'fires only when the collapse is winnable' -- winnable is a claim about the fight that will exist, not the one that exists now.

The arbitration inverts -- the single answer goes to the one bot that will not go.

tpdeathbuy_20260825.why_worth_arming: 验证哲学条件 (c),而且是标准打法不是偏好:Dota 里英雄死亡会把身上未花的金钱按比例赔给击杀者、其余蒸发,**死前把钱花掉**是教科书习惯。块自己的金钱子句正是一条**带**而不是下限(`botGold >= tpCost` 且 `botGold < tpCost + botWorth/40` = 「我买得起,而且我手上这点钱本来就要没」)。TP 卷轴是那里最该买的东西:便宜、用掉而不是掉落、且块只在**手上 TP 不够**时开火。Turbo 里论据更强:复活快,回场的第一件事就是想 TP 回战场。

tpdying_20260819.change: New pure predicate J.IsIncomingBurstLethal(bot, nWindow) -- the same mana/cd-aware estimator J.ShouldRetreatLaneBurst runs over the enemies within 1100, without the laning gate; true when their castable burst already covers the bot's current health. Consumed by ONE new gated release clause inside J.GetTpCommitDefendDesire, immediately after the shipped release: `if J.IsSoakCandidate('tpdying') and J.IsIncomingBurstLethal(bot, 3.0) then release end`. Reachable only inside the existing 'tpcommit' gate, so both shipped play AND today's armed-tpcommit behavior are byte-identical until 'tpdying' is armed.
tpdying_20260819.conservatism: The armed path can only RELEASE a pin (return nil sooner) -- it can never raise or create one, and it cannot fire at all unless 'tpcommit' is armed too. Structurally it cannot add commitment, the same separability argument that let capmono ship ahead of divecap. One lever: the floor VALUE (0.85), the 12s window and the shipped release are all untouched.
tpdying_20260819.defect: J.GetTpCommitDefendDesire pins a fresh TP responder in the answered lane's DEFEND mode with a 0.85 floor, and releases the pin on `J.GetHP(bot) < 0.40 or J.ShouldRetreatLaneBurst(bot)`. The second clause is the ANTICIPATORY one -- the reason the release works at all, since a lander who waits for 40% has already eaten the burst -- but J.ShouldRetreatLaneBurst hard-requires J.IsInLaningPhase() on its third line. The floor is only reachable from the two response-TP branches (J.GetRescueTpTarget / J.ShouldTpSupportTowerFight), which require level 6+ and a >3500u trip, so the frames it actually pins are overwhelmingly POST-laning. There the release degrades to the numeric clause alone: the pin holds until the lander is ALREADY losing. That is the same 'ground down in place' shape (wave12 dossier mechanism D, ~6/24 landing deaths) the release was written against, minus the half that made it work. Same family as GH #29 / #31 / #32: a condition whose DOMAIN does not cover its branch's domain.
tpdying_20260819.mutation_tests: Two. Deleting the gated clause (= pre-fix source) fails exactly the one armed assertion, printing the real pin (got 0.85). Forcing the gate always-on fails exactly the 2 shipped-behavior assertions. 427/427 tests, luacheck bots game 0 warnings.
tpdying_20260819.rationale_c: Two grounds. (1) Internal: the shipped release's own comment states the contract -- '丢失了动手机会才会走', a lander who is dying has lost the chance. This restores that contract in the domain the floor runs in; nothing new is claimed. (2) Standard strategy: whether to hold a contested spot is decided on incoming damage vs effective HP, not on a fixed HP percentage -- a 100% HP support inside a lethal combo should leave, a 45% HP hero out of range should not. Anticipating burst rather than reacting to an HP threshold is the same principle the PROMOTED lanesurv rule already ships on.
tpdying_20260819.scope_note: Audited but NOT changed in this unit, and still owed a final-bid test: midtp/suptp (return BOT_ACTION_DESIRE_HIGH into the item-usage loop, which only tests `> 0` -- the magnitude is inert there, but slot order {5,4,3,2,1,0,15,16} puts the TP scroll LAST, so any other item that wants a frame preempts a response TP), lf_rescue, teambrain, ownhalf, tpwatch. Separately flagged for the replay group: J.GetNearbyLocationToTp resolves a response TP's cast point to 575u in front of the nearest SURVIVING friendly tower and falls back to the fountain, and nothing checks how far that is from the trigger -- while J.WillAllySurviveTpWindow budgets only 4.0s (3s channel + a step), excluding the post-landing walk. That is a candidate mechanical explanation for the 'preconditions all held but it landed at the fountain' lf_rescue frame in replay-check 20260819T033000Z (game 20260819_001937_slot1, t=343.5). Not fixed here -- one lever at a time, and lf_rescue is the variable in the imminent bisect.

tpdying_DOMAIN_CORRECTION_20260820.correction: tpdying's rationale (and GH #35) reads J.IsInLaningPhase as a clock: 'the frames this floor pins are overwhelmingly POST-laning, where the anticipation is structurally dead'. It is not a clock. In turbo it is `t < 8*60` OR `t < 10*60 and GetBot():GetNetWorth() < 8000`, so between 8:00 and 10:00 the answer depends on the RESPONDER'S OWN WALLET -- and under 8000 at nine minutes is the ordinary case, not the exception.
tpdying_DOMAIN_CORRECTION_20260820.effect_on_GH68: GH #68 section 1.1 establishes condition (a) for tpdying by elimination, and its exclusion of the anticipatory clause is 't=556 > 480 (turbo laning floor), so ShouldRetreatLaneBurst structurally returns false'. On that frame it returns... reachable: laning is TRUE at 3068 net worth. So the shipped clause is NOT eliminated. Independently, under the only offline-observable proxy the tpdying predicate reads FALSE on that frame (bristleback 377u + earthshaker 520u dealt 261 into a 504 HP pool) and the pin stays at 0.85 with the id armed. Condition (a) is NOT established; do not spend a wave buying (a) evidence for it on this basis.
tpdying_DOMAIN_CORRECTION_20260820.measured_frames: 20260820_103644 t=492.4 necrolyte (3997 net worth) -> IsInLaningPhase TRUE, J.ShouldRetreatLaneBurst TRUE: the SHIPPED release already drops the pin and arming tpdying is bit-identical (defend 0.1 / retreat 0.75 both ways, real mode files). 20260820_102645 t=556.5 crystal_maiden (3068) -> IsInLaningPhase TRUE. 20260820_102030 t=639.5 tidehunter -> past 10:00, laning FALSE: the premise holds there.
tpdying_DOMAIN_CORRECTION_20260820.negative_result: GH #68 section 5.1 (decouple the comparison from current health, e.g. burst >= HP - 0.40*maxHP) is NOT locally validatable. GetEstimatedDamageToTarget is not in a .dem; the loader substitutes realized damage, which ignores the bCurrentlyAvailable flag -- and that flag IS the mechanism GH #68 section 2.3 blames. On the necro frame the strict comparison already passes (1080 vs 965) so a looser one changes nothing; on the tide frame there is no attributable burst at all. Asserted as a [limitation] case. A corpus carrying the engine estimate is the prerequisite for any threshold work on this id.
tpdying_DOMAIN_CORRECTION_20260820.real_defect_underneath: A SURVIVAL release depending on the responder's own net worth is the sharper statement of the same defect: two landers in one fight, same HP, same enemies, get different releases because one is richer. tpdying happens to remove that dependence, so it is correctly designed and wrongly motivated. Not re-gated this round -- the id already exists and its domain is now measured.

condition_c_reargued.mechanism: A Bone Guard point buys max_skeleton_charges 2/4/6/8 and skeleton damage 34/39/43/49; the COOLDOWN is flat 42s at every rank. X.ConsiderW's only two release branches are thresholds ON THE CAP -- branch 1 `nStack/maxStack >= 0.6`, branch 2 `nStack == maxStack` -- and their only bypass, talent6:IsTrained(), is a level-20 test (GH #84: 0 of 210 turbo hero-slots). So in turbo every Bone Guard point raises, monotonically and on BOTH branches, the absolute bank WK must hold before he releases anything: branch 1 needs 2/3/4/5 charges by rank, branch 2 needs 2/4/6/8. The default row has all four points down by level 7, i.e. from level 7 it asks an 8-charge bank of a hero the batch reads at 15 last hits and 0.6 kills. wkbuild leaves him at cap 2 for the whole laning phase and spends the freed points on the only lockdown he has (2nd Wraithfire Blast point at level 5 instead of 12: stun 1.0->1.2s, cooldown 14->12s) and on maxing Mortal Strike at 8 instead of 10.
condition_c_reargued.strategy_corroboration: Wraithfire Blast is WK's only hard disable and its rank shortens the cooldown 14->12->10->8s; Bone Guard's cooldown is rank-independent (flat 42s). In turbo -- 13-16s respawns, short fight intervals -- cooldown on the only control is the kill-participation lever. Moving points off a non-shortening summon onto the shortening control matches the common public WK skill order (Q/E first, W later).
